property_summary: For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, after play() completes the reference contract either leaves pot incremented (when random==1) or clears pot to 0 and pays out (when random==0); equivalently, when a call results in pot==0 the payout branch must have executed only for the random==0 case — the mutant inverts the condition so there exist inputs (callers/timestamps/block difficulty) that make reference leave a nonzero pot while the mutant clears it (or vice versa), causing c.pot() to differ.

For any caller and block timestamp/difficulty, calling play() with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT never clears pot unless the on-chain RNG value equals 0; the mutant inverts that condition so there exist inputs (caller and block timestamp/difficulty) where the reference leaves pot nonzero but the mutant clears it, making pot() differ.

For every call to play with msg.value == TICKET_AMOUNT, the original contract only clears pot (sets pot to 0) when the computed on-chain random equals 0; the mutant inverts that check so there exist inputs (caller and block timestamp/prevRandao) where the mutant clears pot but the original does not, causing c.pot() to differ.

For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract only clears pot (sets pot to 0) when its computed on-chain random == 0; the mutant inverts the check so there exist inputs (block.timestamp/block.difficulty and caller) where the mutant clears pot while the reference does not, making pot differ.

For any caller who pays exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract C only transfers the fee to bank and resets pot to 0 when its internal RNG equals 0; the mutant inverts the RNG check so there exist caller/timestamp/difficulty inputs for which the mutant clears pot (and pays the fee) while the reference does not, causing c.pot() to differ.

For any call to play sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, if the caller wins (so pot is paid out) the reference contract always resets pot to 0 at the end of the call; the mutant leaves pot equal to FEE_AMOUNT after a win, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any valid play() call that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, if the caller wins the round then the reference contract always resets pot to 0 after completion; the mutant incorrectly leaves pot equal to FEE_AMOUNT for some winning calls, so there exist inputs where pot != 0 after a winning play.

For every successful play() that transfers out the pot (i.e. when the contract sends TICKET_AMOUNT and then pays winner and fee in the same call), the reference contract always sets pot to 0 afterwards; the mutant sometimes leaves pot equal to FEE_AMOUNT after such a payout, so there exists a caller/address and block context where address(c).balance and c.pot() diverge from the expected post-payout state (specifically pot != 0).

After any successful play that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and results in a payout (random == 0), the reference contract always sets pot to 0 at the end of the call; the mutant leaves pot == FEE_AMOUNT for some inputs, so there exist fuzzed caller and block timestamp/difficulty contexts that make c.pot() != 0 only on the mutant.

For any admissible play() call that sends exactly the ticket amount, if the call results in a payout (the contract transfers out the pot), then the reference contract always resets pot to 0 at the end of the call; the mutant erroneously leaves pot equal to FEE_AMOUNT for some inputs, so there exist fuzzed inputs where c.pot() != 0 after a payout.

For any play() call that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and results in a win, the reference contract transfers the full pot minus FEE_AMOUNT to the winner and resets pot to 0 after transfers; the mutant that sets pot = 0 before transfers causes the winner's payout calculation to be wrong (zero or too small) and changes final pot, so there exists an input (a caller that wins) that makes pot differ.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), after the call the contract's pot is always 0 in the correct contract (because on a win the pot is paid out and then reset) — the mutant that resets pot before transfers can leave pot non-zero (or alter payouts), so there exists a caller and call that makes c.pot() differ between reference and mutant.

For any caller who sends exactly the ticket amount to play(), if play() completes then the contract's pot is zero (the reference empties pot after paying winner), whereas the mutant that sets pot = 0 before transfers can leave pot different or change transfer amounts, so there exists a caller/seed where pot differs.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), if the call does not revert then the contract's pot is always 0 after the call in the reference; the mutant that zeroes pot before transfers can leave pot non-zero (or change transfers) for some caller, so the property distinguishes them.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), if the call succeeds then the contract's balance equals its public pot (i.e., address(c).balance == c.pot()), a relationship the reference preserves but the mutant can break by zeroing pot before making transfers which changes pot while balance has already been reduced by transfers.

For any single call to play() sending the required ticket amount, the reference contract always sets pot to 0 whenever the caller wins (random==0); the mutant that omits resetting pot leaves pot > 0 after a winning play for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For every play() call that pays the exact ticket amount and where the caller wins (random==0), the reference contract always resets pot to 0 after the call; the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot > 0 for some inputs, so the post-call pot==0 invariant is violated.

For any single valid play() call that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT from any caller, if the caller wins (random==0) then the reference contract always sets pot to 0 after the call; the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot > 0 for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), if the caller wins (random == 0) then the reference contract transfers winnings and ensures the contract's pot becomes 0 after the call; the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot > 0 for some fuzzed inputs where the caller wins.

For any call to play sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract always makes pot either unchanged (if caller loses) or exactly 0 after the call (if caller wins); the mutant can leave pot strictly greater than 0 after a winning call, so there exist inputs (sender + block state) where pot != 0 post-call.

For every call to play with the ticket amount exactly equal to TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract accepts the call (updates pot and may pay out) while the mutant rejects it; i.e., calls with msg.value == TICKET_AMOUNT should NOT revert on the reference but do revert on the mutant that requires msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT.

For every nonzero ETH payment not equal to the ticket amount, C.accepts the call (does not revert) and increases its pot by that payment when random branch doesn't payout immediately; the mutant that flips the require to msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT will reject exactly the ticket amount instead, so fuzzing payment values distinguishes them (we assert that when sending a value different from TICKET_AMOUNT the call to play does not revert and address(c).balance increases accordingly).

For every call to play with msg.value equal to the required ticket amount, the reference accepts the call (does not revert) while the mutant that flips the require to msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT will revert for that same input; thus the reference always allows msg.value == TICKET_AMOUNT but the mutant rejects it.

For every call to play with any msg.value, the reference C never reverts (it only requires equality to TICKET_AMOUNT which the fuzzer will satisfy or else the call reverts) — tighten domain to only values NOT equal to TICKET_AMOUNT so reference and mutant differ in whether they accept those values: the reference reverts when msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT, while the mutant accepts them; therefore for all admissible inputs (msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT) the reference will revert (call fails) but the mutant will succeed, so asserting that play reverts for msg.value != TICKET_AMOUNT holds for the reference and is violated by the mutant for some input.

For any caller and payment of exactly 10 wei, the correct contract C always resets pot to 0 whenever its internal pseudorandom bit equals 0 (i.e., the contract pays out and clears the pot); the mutant flips the condition and therefore for some inputs (those that make the random bit 0) the mutant fails to clear the pot while the reference clears it.

For any caller and any valid ticket payment, the reference contract either pays out and resets pot to 0 whenever its pseudorandom bit equals 0; the mutant flips the condition so there exist inputs (caller + block state yielding random==0) where the mutant does not reset pot — we assert that after play the pot is either unchanged or zero in the reference but the mutant can leave pot non-zero when reference cleared it.

For any caller paying the exact ticket amount, after calling play the reference contract C either leaves pot unchanged (when no payout) or clears pot to 0 (when payout occurs); the mutant flips the payout condition so there exist inputs (block timestamp/difficulty/caller producing random==0) where the reference clears pot to 0 but the mutant leaves pot non-zero.

For any caller who pays the exact ticket amount, if the reference contract C clears the pot to zero immediately after play (i.e., payout occurred), then the caller's balance after the call is strictly greater than before the call by (pot_before - FEE_AMOUNT); the mutant flips the payout condition and for some inputs C clears pot but mutant does not, breaking this relation.

For any caller paying the exact ticket amount, after calling play the contract's pot is never negative and, moreover, the reference implementation guarantees that whenever the pseudorandom bit equals 0 the pot is reset to 0 (i.e., address(c).balance reflects that payout happened and pot became 0); the mutant flipping the condition (random==1) allows an input (same caller and block state producing random==0) where the reference clears the pot but the mutant does not, so asserting address(c).balance decreased by the payout amount (or pot==0) distinguishes them.

For any caller paying exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and causing the contract to reset the pot (the winning branch), the reference always sends the FEE_AMOUNT to the bank so that address(c).balance increases by FEE_AMOUNT, whereas the mutant sometimes sends that fee to the player instead, so address(c).balance will not increase by FEE_AMOUNT for some inputs (player addresses and randomness).

For every play call that wins (random==0) the reference contract always increases its own contract balance by FEE_AMOUNT (the bank receives the fee), while the mutant sometimes does not (it sends the fee to the player), so address(c).balance >= FEE_AMOUNT after a winning play for the reference but not always for the mutant.

For every admissible play call that wins (random == 0), the reference C always leaves the bank address (bank) with +FEE_AMOUNT meaning address(c).balance does NOT increase by the fee (bank gets it) while the mutant sometimes transfers the fee to msg.sender causing address(c).balance and/or bank balance differences; equivalently, after a winning play the reference preserves that the contract's pot is reset to 0 and the contract's own balance is unchanged by the fee (i.e., address(c).balance == 0 after payouts when caller had only supplied exactly TICKET_AMOUNT), a property broken by the mutant when it pays the fee to the player instead of bank resulting in address(c).balance != 0 in some cases.

For any caller and block state, when play() is invoked with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and the play results in a win (random==0), the reference implementation always transfers FEE_AMOUNT to the bank address (so bank's balance increases by FEE_AMOUNT), while the mutant that transfers the fee to msg.sender will in some cases fail to increase bank's balance by FEE_AMOUNT; the test asserts bank's balance increased by FEE_AMOUNT after a winning play.

For any caller and admissible block state, if play() is called with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT then after the call the contract's public pot is zero (the pot is emptied on a winning play) — the mutant still sets pot=0 but the observable difference is that the contract's balance increases by FEE_AMOUNT in the reference when the blockchain delivers the payout to the bank via payable(bank).transfer, while the mutant sometimes sends the fee to msg.sender so address(c).balance will NOT always increase by FEE_AMOUNT; therefore the general rule we assert is: when a caller sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and the call completes, address(c).balance is either unchanged or equals zero except in the specific winning-and-fee-kept-by-bank case where address(c).balance increases by FEE_AMOUNT — equivalently we assert that after play() completes, either pot==0 and address(c).balance >= 0 holds and specifically that if pot==0 then address(c).balance % 1 == 0 (trivially true) — to craft a precise distinguishing universal property we assert that after a play with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the contract's pot is zero (which the reference always ensures) and the test will fail on the mutant for some fuzzed inputs because the mutant redirects the fee to the player causing balances to differ.

After any single call to play with the correct ticket payment, the reference contract resets pot to 0 whenever it pays out a winner, but the mutant that omits resetting pot may leave a nonzero pot after a winning payout; the rule: for any caller and admissible ticket payment, if play() completes then either pot==TICKET_AMOUNT (only the just-paid ticket remains) or pot==0 in the reference whenever a payout occurred — concretely: after a play by any player sending exactly 10 wei, the reference never leaves pot > 10, while the mutant can leave pot > 10.

For any caller who pays exactly the ticket amount (10 wei) to play(), after the call completes the reference never increases the contract pot beyond the single ticket amount when a payout happened (i.e. pot is either 0 or exactly 10), but the mutant that fails to reset pot can leave pot > 10 for some sequence of plays and callers.

For any single call to play() paying exactly the ticket amount, the reference C ensures the contract pot is at most the ticket amount after the call completes (it never accumulates previous pots across a winning payout), whereas the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot larger than the ticket amount for some sequence of plays and callers.

After any single call to play() where the caller sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract ensures that if the contract paid out the caller (i.e., the caller received more than the ticket back) then the contract's pot is 0; the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot > 0 after such a payout.

For any single play call paying exactly the ticket amount, the reference contract guarantees that the contract balance (address(c).balance) after the call is at most the ticket amount (either 0 or the freshly-paid ticket), while the mutant that fails to reset pot can leave the contract balance greater than the ticket amount for some input sequences (fuzzer will find an input ordering of two distinct players to demonstrate this).

After any successful play() call that wins (random==0), the contract's pot is zero in the reference implementation for all inputs; the mutant increments pot before payout causing the winner payout amount to differ and still leaves pot at zero but the transfer amount becomes incorrect — this can be detected by comparing address(c).balance change of the caller vs expected (i.e., caller's balance increases by pot_before - FEE), and the mutant breaks that for some fuzzed caller/state.

If a caller sends exactly the ticket amount and the randomized branch pays out (random==0), then the reference always transfers to the caller exactly the pot (including their ticket) minus the fixed fee, while the mutant (which increments pot extra before payout) can cause the transferred amount to be larger; we assert that after a winning play the caller's balance increases by pot_before - FEE and address(c).balance decreases accordingly.

For any caller who sends exactly the ticket price and triggers a winning payout, the reference contract always transfers to the caller exactly the pot prior to payout minus the fixed fee (and leaves c.pot == 0); the mutant that increments pot before payout can make the transferred amount larger, violating that invariant for some inputs.
